title: Vicarious pain experiences in healthy and chronic pain samples.
summary:
The word “vicarious” means “substituting for another”. Vicarious pain describes a phenomenon, where people experience first-hand pain sensations upon observing other people in pain.

Experiencing vicarious pain may be associated with an increased psychological burden and a poorer overall sense of well-being. This appears to be especially relevant for individuals with chronic pain who regularly encounter others in pain, such as in doctors' practices or self-help groups. Given that around 28% of the German population have chronic pain and that for about 2.2 million Germans this is already associated with a severe psychological burden, in this study we would like to investigate the influence of chronic pain on the experience of vicarious pain.

So far only little research has been done on vicarious pain, and it remains unclear whether there is a general relationship between chronic pain and vicarious pain.
For this reason, we want to examine people with chronic pain within an online survey-study using questionnaires, especially regarding their chronic pain and experiences of vicarious pain, as well as empathy and prosocial behavior.

interventions.name: Participants with chronic pain fill out questionnaires online about their pain, vicarious pain, empathy and prosocial behavior.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Fluent in German
- Chronic pain (defined as at least 15 pain days per month for the past three months)
- Voluntary consent to participate
Exclusion criteria:
- Regular use of illicit drugs in the past six months (defined as weekly or (nearly) daily use of cocaine, stimulants, inhalants, hallucinogens or narcotics)
- Participation in the currently ongoing experimental study with the acronym SOPA1 (DRKS00037736)
- Acute infections at the time of study participation (e.g. cold symptoms)
